crop.notes: Only the first column of the 'Fistiana' report: headlines, the men, the start, the ring and rules 1-4. It ends mid-rule 5; the article continues in the next columns (rounds 1-24 are not clipped) and ends in article 303's clipping.

ocr.notes: Headlines and most of the text readable; the Reddish family and rules sections are badly garbled.

summary.suggested: The Daily Missouri Democrat reported that Tom Allen beat Bill Davis for $1,000 in 43 rounds and 41 minutes on Chouteau Island near Rhodes' Point, his first fight in America, with profiles of both men.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'Daily Democrat', Wednesday morning, Jan. 13, 1869. Before the 1875 merger, so not the Globe-Democrat.

facts.fact: Allen beat Bill Davis for $1,000 in 43 rounds and 41 minutes on Chouteau Island near Rhodes' Point, about twelve miles above St. Louis, where McCoole and Davis had fought in 1866
places: Chouteau Island, near Rhodes' Point, about 12 miles above St. Louis

facts.fact: The paper said Allen was born at Birmingham, England, in 1841 and was 28 years old
Allen had been in America eighteen months, and the Davis fight was his first in America
In England Allen's principal fights were with Waggoner, White Clark, Tony Gould, Bingey Rose, J. Parkinson, P. Price, George Jils, Joe Goss and Bob Smith; Smith won, and Allen won most of the others
Allen boarded the steamer Henry Adkins at Venice, Illinois, with his trainer Tom Kelley on the way to the fight

notes: The birth year is printed as '1841' (slightly smudged) and his age as 28, which conflicts with fact 001 (1839). Height '5 feet 9 1/2', weight 160-175 pounds. Allen's seconds were Wm. Ryall and Tom Kelley; Wm. Collins was referee. Davis was born in Belfast in 1832. Article 303 is the end of this same report.
